listenings.text: Good morning, everybody, and welcome to day one. Two changes to the program before you go anywhere. First, the buyer meeting room has moved from hall two to hall four. Hall four, not hall two. Second, the panel on export rules now starts at eleven thirty, not at eleven, so you have half an hour more than you thought. Next, a reminder for the exhibitors. Every visitor badge here can be scanned at any booth. Please scan the badge instead of collecting business cards, because the contact details arrive already typed and you will not spend Friday night reading somebody's handwriting. And one piece of advice, from people who have done this for years. Do not close your booth early. The serious buyers walk the floor after four o'clock, when the crowd is gone and they can finally hear themselves think. The last hour is the best hour. Have a good show.

I have run a booth at about twenty of these, and I will tell you the one thing almost everybody gets wrong. They present. Somebody stops, and they talk about their own company for two minutes, beautifully, and at the end of those two minutes they know absolutely nothing about the person who was standing in front of them. And that person walks away and never comes back. My first two questions are always the same. Where are you based, and who do you buy this category from today. That is it. The first one tells me if they can even use what I sell, and the second one tells me whose business I would be taking, which is the only interesting question at a trade fair. And one last thing about leads, because people love to count them. Sixty leads that nobody follows up on are worth less than four that somebody actually calls on Monday morning. The fair is not the work. The Monday after it is the work.
